source.title: Emergence and Evolution of Interpretable Concepts in Diffusion Models
source.authors: Berk Tınaz; Zalan Fabian; M. Soltanolkotabi

page_placements.theme: Optimisation and data-statistics artifact latents (dense, unigram, position-locked)

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains SAEs and analyzes their concepts, but does not compare dictionary sizes or test whether larger-dictionary features split, align with smaller features, or partition their activations. Its results concern concept changes over diffusion time, not feature splitting by SAE size.
record.gate_note: The study reports SAE concept cohesion and separability across diffusion timesteps, and qualitative observations of spatially localized context-free activations. It does not report results on increasing dictionary size, matched feature directions across sizes, or partitions of coarse-feature inputs. Other segmentation and intervention results concern diffusion composition and editing, not the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study trains TopK SAEs of one size (nf = 5120) on Stable Diffusion v1.4 activations and compares concepts across diffusion timesteps, not dictionary sizes. It never varies dictionary size or tests parent/child latents, absorption or alternative objectives. 'Feature splitting' is never named; Bricken et al. is cited only as background on SAE training. The record's 'discusses' overstates the link; 'cites_only' fits better. Either way it does not test the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors conclude that scene layout emerges at the first reverse diffusion step and is largely fixed by mid-trajectory. They find SAE-feature interventions control composition early and style mid-trajectory, and concepts become purer and more distinct over time. They draw no conclusion on feature splitting.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains TopK SAEs on Stable Diffusion v1.4 residual updates and compares concepts across diffusion timesteps, not across dictionary sizes; it does not test the feature-splitting recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Diffusion timestep changes the reported Word2Vec-based cohesion and separability values.

fits_no_version.finding: Word2Vec concept cohesion rises from 0.588 (t = 1.0) to 0.664 (t = 0.0); pairwise similarity falls from 0.433 to 0.344.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE concepts in diffusion models become more cohesive and distinct over the reverse diffusion trajectory.

fits_no_version.finding: Some latents fire in fixed spatial regions regardless of semantics; the authors hypothesise they are optimization artifacts that reduce reconstruction error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: TopK SAEs on diffusion activations learn semantics-independent, position-locked latents as reconstruction knobs.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix D notes redundant semantic concepts firing in the same region, which the authors speculate add different conceptual layers (e.g. food and round). This is qualitative and at a single SAE size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multiple SAE latents co-fire on the same image region, possibly encoding different attributes.

record.problems: The feature-geometry question is not tested: SAEs are trained separately for each timestep, and the paper notes that concepts across timesteps are not directly comparable. The reported cohesion and separability metrics use Word2Vec label embeddings rather than SAE feature directions.
record.rows_left_out: Segmentation-accuracy and intervention outcomes in Sections 4.2–4.3 and Appendix E.2 are about image composition prediction and editing, not feature splitting or cross-size SAE relations, so they are not included.

untested.parts: No variation of dictionary size; only nf = 5120.
No cross-size or cross-family splitting analysis; only Stable Diffusion v1.4.
No nested feature families or hierarchy geometry between latents.
No comparison of latents between SAE sizes.
No alternative objective (e.g. Matryoshka) and no test that splitting is an objective artifact.

record.verdict_notes: Changed relation from 'discusses' to 'cites_only': the paper never discusses feature splitting. The Appendix D remark on redundant co-firing concepts is too qualitative, and at one SAE size, to bear on V3 or V4.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison across SAE dictionary sizes or test of whether multiple larger-SAE features cover a smaller feature's inputs and lie near its direction.
Only Stable Diffusion v1.4 is studied; there is no test of feature splitting at scale or across SAE families or open SAE releases.
The paper does not test nested feature families or geometric relationships between features across SAE sizes. Its temporal concept metrics use separately trained SAEs and Word2Vec concept labels.
No parent-child feature takeover or absorption test, nor a size or sparsity intervention aimed at that phenomenon.
No comparison of larger- and smaller-SAE latents, combinations of latents, or novel latents across dictionary sizes.
No test of whether the SAE objective produces splitting, and no comparison with Matryoshka SAEs or another objective.

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion v1.4
rows.operation_detail: Measured concept cohesion using Word2Vec labels in the concept dictionary.
rows.note: This measures distances of dictionary-word embeddings from their concept centers, not distances or alignments between SAE feature directions across dictionary sizes.
rows.check: Word2Vec cohesion of concept-dictionary labels at one SAE size; does not measure splitting across dictionary sizes.

rows.operation_detail: Measured pairwise concept separability using Word2Vec concept-center embeddings.
rows.note: The measure is average pairwise cosine similarity of concept-label embeddings; it is not a cross-size feature-geometry measure.

relation.reason: It cites Bricken et al. [2] only as the first ReLU+L1 SAE approach, in related work, and never discusses feature splitting.

tranche.reason: The study uses a single SAE size (nf = 4d = 5120). It never varies dictionary size or tests splitting, absorption or other objectives. Feature splitting is never mentioned.

source_check.notes: The only related content is the qualitative context-free latents (Appendix D, Appendix G, Figures 17-18). The authors hypothesise these are optimization artifacts that reduce reconstruction error. This is not evidence on feature splitting. There are no verdicts.
